mainTopic: עיקר וטפל, the praise of ארץ ישראל's fruit, and the after-blessing for fruits and grains (ברכה אחת מעין שלש)
overview: The amud opens with a משנה about עיקר וטפל: one ברכה on the main food covers a secondary food eaten with it, even bread eaten alongside salted food. The גמרא explains that this happens with the very sweet פירות גינוסר, where salty food balances the sweetness and bread only helps with the salty food. It then tells exaggerated stories praising פירות גינוסר and the abundance of ארץ ישראל. These include ינאי המלך's huge harvests on הר המלך and the eighty priestly couples of גופנית. רב and רבי יוחנן add what a meal needs to count as a real meal: salt, or a cooked dish with gravy. A new משנה follows. רבן גמליאל requires full ברכת המזון after grapes, figs and pomegranates, the חכמים require one blessing summarizing the three, and רבי עקיבא and רבי טרפון add their own rulings. The גמרא explains how each side reads the verses, rules that grain foods and the שבעת המינים get ברכה אחת מעין שלש afterward, and gives its wording. It ends by settling the closing line: after a reversal, 'ועל פירותיה' is said in ארץ ישראל and 'ועל הפירות' outside it.

steps.title: Salted food comes first and bread with it
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that if salted food is the main item and bread is eaten with it, one makes a ברכה only on the salted food, and that ברכה covers the bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If they brought him salted food first, and bread with it, he makes a ברכה on the salted food and that exempts the bread, because the bread is secondary to it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a case where bread, normally the most important food, is only a side item. The ברכה goes on the salted food instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually פת is the most important food, and its ברכה covers everything else. Here it is reversed: the bread is eaten only to help with the salty food. So the bread is טפל, and the ברכה on the salted food covers it.

keyTerms.meaning: Exempts; one ברכה covers the other food
Secondary; eaten only to help the main food

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think bread lost its status as bread in general. It is still bread, with its normal ברכה. Only in this specific setting it is eaten as a side item, so it is covered by the ברכה on the main food.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: If they brought before him salted food first
and bread with it —
he recites a blessing over the salted food
and exempts the bread,
because the bread is secondary to it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵבִיאוּ לְפָנָיו מָלִיחַ תְּחִלָּה וּפַת עִמּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opening of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When salted food is the main item, its ברכה covers the bread eaten with it.

steps.title: The general rule of main and secondary foods
steps.stepSummary: The משנה turns the case into a general rule: whenever one food is the main item and another is secondary, the ברכה on the main item covers the secondary.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the rule: whenever there is a main food with a secondary food alongside it, you make a ברכה on the main food and that exempts the secondary food.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה turns the specific case into a general principle that applies to any food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The salted-food case is one example of a wider rule. What counts is the food's role in the meal, not how important it usually is. Whatever is eaten only to serve the main food is covered by the main food's ברכה.
steps.whatToRemember: The rule of עיקר וטפל: one ברכה on the main food covers the secondary food. Even bread can be טפל if it is eaten only to support something else.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic rule in הלכות ברכות and is used in practice all the time, for example a cracker eaten with a dip or a chaser after a drink.

phrases.english: This is the principle:
anything that is primary, with a secondary food alongside it —
one recites a blessing over the primary
and exempts the secondary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the specific case into a general principle
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ברכה on the עיקר exempts the טפל.

steps.title: Can salted food really be the main food over bread?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה's case: is there ever a situation where salted food is the main item and bread is only secondary?
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Is there really any situation where salted food is the main item and bread is secondary?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions whether the משנה's example could happen in real life. This sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally nobody makes a meal out of salty food and eats bread just as a side. So the משנה's case seems unrealistic. The גמרא needs a real-life situation that fits it.

keyTerms.meaning: Is there really such a thing?

phrases.english: GEMARA: And is there anything
where salted food is primary and bread is secondary?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how the משנה's case could happen
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's case of מליח עיקר ופת טפלה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Bread is normally the most important part of a meal, so it is hard to imagine it as secondary to salted food.

steps.title: The case is about people eating פירות גינוסר
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב עוירא, quoting רב אשי, explains that the משנה is speaking about people eating the extremely sweet פירות גינוסר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא, son of רב עוירא, said in the name of רב אשי: The משנה is talking about people who eat the fruits of גינוסר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by giving a real situation where salty food is the main item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פירות גינוסר were so sweet that people ate salty food afterward to balance the sweetness. Then they ate bread only to make the salty food easier to eat. In that setting the salty food is the main item, and the bread really is secondary.

keyTerms.meaning: The famously sweet fruits of the גינוסר valley near the Kinneret

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's unusual case happens with פירות גינוסר: salty food balances the sweet fruit, and bread is eaten only to help with the salty food.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב עַוִּירָא
phrases.english: Rav Aḥa, son of Rav Avira, said
that Rav Ashi said:
They taught this about those who eat fruits of Genosar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by identifying a realistic case
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case to a specific situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed bread could never be secondary to salted food.
steps.terutzMaskana: With the very sweet פירות גינוסר, salty food becomes the main item and bread only supports it.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's huge appetite for פירות גינוסר
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה tells an exaggerated story: his group brought רבי יוחנן enormous amounts of פירות גינוסר, he ate them all, and he swore he had not tasted any food.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said: When we used to go with רבי יוחנן to eat פירות גינוסר, if we were a hundred people, each of us brought him ten. If we were ten people, each of us brought him a hundred. Every hundred fruits filled a basket of three סאה. He ate them all and swore he had not tasted any food.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that פירות גינוסר have been mentioned, the גמרא moves into stories praising them. This story is a deliberate exaggeration.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Either way the group brought him a thousand fruits, and every hundred filled a large basket. The point is how delicious and light the fruit was: even after so much, רבי יוחנן did not feel he had eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא famous for amazing, exaggerated stories

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a halachic step and not a literal record. It is אגדה using exaggeration to praise the fruit.

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֲוָה אָזְלִינַן בָּתְרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
phrases.english: When we would go after Rabbi Yoḥanan
to eat fruits of Genosar,
when we were a hundred people —

phrases.aramaic: מְנַקְּטִינַן לֵיהּ לְכֹל חַד וְחַד עַשְׂרָה עַשְׂרָה,
phrases.english: each and every one of us would bring him ten,
and when we were ten people,

phrases.aramaic: מְנַקְּטִינַן לֵיהּ כֹּל חַד וְחַד מְאָה מְאָה.
phrases.english: each and every one of us would bring him a hundred.
And every hundred of them

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה מַחֲזִיק לְהוּ צַנָּא בַּר תְּלָתָא סָאוֵי
phrases.english: would fill a basket holding three se'a
and he would eat them,
and swear that he had not tasted food.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הֲוָה אָזְלִינַן בָּתְרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְמֵיכַל פֵּירוֹת גִּנּוֹסַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Side discussion praising the fruit just mentioned
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Story: פירות גינוסר were so good that רבי יוחנן ate huge amounts and felt he had eaten nothing.

steps.title: Could he really say he tasted no food at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects to the wording: how could רבי יוחנן swear he tasted no food after eating so much?
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really think he said he had not tasted food?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the exact word used in the story. This sets up a correction of the wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He obviously ate a great deal, so swearing he tasted no food would be a false oath. The word זיונא cannot be taken literally.

phrases.english: Does it enter your mind that he said he tasted no food?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the story
steps.kashyaTarget: The word זיונא in רבי יוחנן's oath
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He clearly ate food, so swearing he ate none would be impossible.

steps.title: Correct the word to מזונא, real filling food
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the wording: he swore he had not tasted מזונא, meaning food that satisfies.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: he had not tasted מזונא (filling food).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the problem by changing the word. He meant that the fruit did not fill him up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מזונא means food that gives real satisfaction. The fruit was delicious but did not satisfy him, so his oath was true.

phrases.english: Rather, say "sustenance."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the wording challenge
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He swore he ate no food at all, which is impossible.
steps.terutzMaskana: He swore he was not satisfied, which is true.

steps.title: How רבי אבהו, רב אמי and רב אסי ate the fruit
steps.stepSummary: More exaggerated praise: רבי אבהו ate until a fly slid off his forehead, and רב אמי and רב אסי ate until their hair fell out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו ate until a fly would slip off his forehead. רב אמי and רב אסי ate until their hair fell out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the stories praising פירות גינוסר, showing what happened to other חכמים who ate them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each line shows the fruit's strong effect. רבי אבהו's skin became so smooth that a fly slid off, and רב אמי and רב אסי ate so much their hair fell out. It is exaggeration meant to praise the fruit.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu ate

phrases.aramaic: עַד דַּהֲוָה שָׁרֵיק לֵיהּ דּוּדְבָא מֵאַפּוּתֵיהּ.
phrases.english: until a fly would slip off his forehead.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב אַמֵּי וְרַב אַסִּי הֲווֹ אָכְלִי
phrases.english: And Rav Ami and Rav Asi would eat
until their hair fell out.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָכֵיל עַד דַּהֲוָה שָׁרֵיק לֵיהּ דּוּדְבָא מֵאַפּוּתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the stories praising פירות גינוסר
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Further stories of חכמים showing the strong effect of פירות גינוסר.

steps.title: ריש לקיש loses his clarity and is brought home
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש ate the fruit until he became confused. רבי יוחנן told the נשיא's household, and רבי יהודה נשיאה sent officers to bring him home.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש would eat until he became confused. רבי יוחנן would tell the household of the נשיא, and רבי יהודה נשיאה would send officers after him, and they would bring him to his house.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last story here praising פירות גינוסר. It shows the fruit was so overwhelming that ריש לקיש had to be escorted home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story goes one step further than the earlier ones: the fruit affected ריש לקיש's mind. It also shows the care around him, since רבי יוחנן alerted the נשיא and officers took him home safely.

keyTerms.meaning: Until he became confused / lost his clarity

steps.whatToRemember: These stories are אגדה praising the sweetness of פירות גינוסר. They connect back to the halachic point: this fruit was so sweet that people ate salty food after it, which is why the משנה could treat salted food as the עיקר.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ הֲוָה אָכֵיל עַד דְּמָרֵיד.
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish would eat until he became confused.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר לְהוּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לִדְבֵי נְשִׂיאָה
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan would tell the household of the Nasi,

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲוָה מְשַׁדַּר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה נְשִׂיאָה
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yehuda Nesia would send
officers after him,
and they would bring him to his house.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ הֲוָה אָכֵיל עַד דְּמָרֵיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final story in the series praising פירות גינוסר
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Story: ריש לקיש was so affected by the fruit that he had to be escorted home by the נשיא's officers.

steps.title: ינאי המלך's city and its huge supply of salted fish
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports that one city of ינאי המלך on הר המלך sent out 600,000 bowls of salted fish every week for the workers cutting figs.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came from ארץ ישראל, he said: ינאי המלך had one city on הר המלך. Every week, from one Friday to the next, they sent out of it six hundred thousand bowls of salted fish for the workers cutting figs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps telling stories that praise how much fruit ארץ ישראל produced. This one comes from רב דימי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The workers needed salted fish to balance all the sweet figs they were eating. So the number of fish bowls shows how many workers there were and how many figs grew. This story also sets up the coming statement about salt in a meal.

keyTerms.meaning: When [he] came. Used for a sage arriving in Bavel from ארץ ישראל with a report.
The King's Mountain, a fertile royal region in ארץ ישראל
A small salted fish, like a sardine

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said:
phrases.notes: He came from ארץ ישראל to Bavel.

phrases.aramaic: עִיר אַחַת הָיְתָה לוֹ לְיַנַּאי הַמֶּלֶךְ
phrases.english: King Yannai had one city
on the King's Mountain,
from which they would take out
six hundred thousand bowls of salted fish
for the fig-cutters
phrases.notes: The workers harvesting figs.

phrases.english: from Shabbat eve to Shabbat eve.
phrases.notes: That is, every single week.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of stories praising the fruit of ארץ ישראל
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The fig harvest on הר המלך was so huge that 600,000 bowls of salted fish were needed every week for the workers.

steps.title: ינאי המלך's tree full of young pigeons
steps.stepSummary: רבין reports that from one tree of ינאי המלך they took down forty סאה of young pigeons each month, from three broods.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין came, he said: ינאי המלך had one tree on הר המלך. Every month they took down from it forty סאה of young pigeons, from three broods.
steps.whatsHappening: Another visitor from ארץ ישראל, רבין, adds one more amazing report about הר המלך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the praise is about birds, not fruit. A single tree held enough nests to produce forty סאה of chicks every month. It is still the same theme: the overflowing blessing of ארץ ישראל.
steps.confusionAlert: Some translations (including Sefaria's) say 'רב דימי' here. Our text clearly says רָבִין, a different visitor from ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: When Ravin came, he said:

phrases.aramaic: אִילָן אֶחָד הָיָה לוֹ לְיַנַּאי הַמֶּלֶךְ
phrases.english: King Yannai had one tree
on the King's Mountain,
from which they would bring down
forty se'a of young pigeons
from three broods each month.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel report about ינאי המלך's holdings on הר המלך
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A single tree on הר המלך produced forty סאה of young pigeons every month.

steps.title: The city of גופנית and its eighty pairs of כהנים brothers
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק reports a city called גופנית where eighty pairs of brothers who were כהנים married eighty pairs of sisters who were כהנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי יצחק came, he said: There was a city in ארץ ישראל called גופנית. In it, eighty pairs of brothers who were כהנים were married to eighty pairs of sisters from כהנים families.
steps.whatsHappening: A third visitor, רבי יצחק, praises ארץ ישראל in a new way: by how many families and כהנים lived in one city.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two כהן brothers marrying two sisters who are daughters of a כהן is rare. Finding eighty such pairs in one city shows how crowded and blessed the land was. The next step will show just how unusual this was.

keyTerms.meaning: Gufnit, a city in ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: When Rabbi Yitzchak came, he said:
There was one city in the Land of Israel
and its name was Gufnit,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהָיוּ בָּהּ שְׁמֹנִים זוּגוֹת אַחִים כֹּהֲנִים
phrases.english: in which there were eighty pairs of brothers who were priests
married to eighty pairs of sisters from priestly families.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third report praising ארץ ישראל, this time about its people rather than its produce
steps.mimraCoreRuling: גופנית had eighty pairs of כהן brothers married to eighty pairs of כהנת sisters.

steps.title: The רבנן search בבל and find barely one similar case
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן searched from סורא to נהרדעא and found only רב חסדא's daughters, married to two brothers. Even there, the brothers were not כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן searched from סורא all the way to נהרדעא and found nothing like it. The only case they found was the daughters of רב חסדא, who were married to רמי בר חמא and מר עוקבא בר חמא. And even there, the women were from a כהן family, but the men were not כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how amazing the report about גופנית was by comparing it to Bavel. Across all of Bavel, not even one complete match could be found.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two sisters married to two brothers turned up only once, with רב חסדא's daughters. Even that case was only half a match, because the husbands were not כהנים. So eighty full pairs in one city is truly remarkable.

keyTerms.meaning: Sura, a major Torah center in Bavel
Neharde'a, another major Torah center in Bavel

phrases.english: And the Sages checked from Sura to Neharde'a
and did not find [such a case]
except for the daughters of Rav Chisda,
who were married to Rami bar Chama
and to Mar Ukva bar Chama.
phrases.notes: The two husbands were brothers.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּאִינְהִי הֲווֹ כָּהֲנָתָא,
phrases.english: And even though they (the women) were from a priestly family,
phrases.notes: רב חסדא was a כהן.

phrases.english: they (the men) were not priests.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how rare the גופנית situation was by comparing it with Bavel
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even across all of Bavel, there was not one full parallel to the eighty pairs in גופנית.
steps.whatToRemember: The stories of ארץ ישראל's abundance end here. Its fruit, its birds and its people were all blessed beyond what was found anywhere else.

steps.title: A meal without salt is not a real meal
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that any meal with no salt does not count as a proper meal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: Any meal that has no salt in it is not a meal.
steps.whatsHappening: The salted fish from step 10 leads the גמרא to a new short topic: what a meal needs in order to count as a real meal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב teaches that salt is a basic part of any proper meal. Without it, the eating does not have the standing of a true סעודה. This matches the idea that salty food was needed to balance all the sweet fruit.

phrases.english: Rav said:
Any meal in which there is no salt
is not a meal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: כׇּל סְעוּדָה שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ מֶלַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the theme of salted food from the fig-cutters story
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A meal without salt does not count as a meal.

steps.title: A meal without a cooked dish with gravy is not a real meal
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, through רבי חייא בר אבא, rules that a meal without שריף is not a proper meal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Any meal that has no שריף in it is not a meal.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion on the same question: what makes a meal complete. Here the answer is שריף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רש"י, שריף is a cooked dish with gravy or broth. רב pointed to salt, and רבי יוחנן points to a cooked, saucy dish. Both are teaching what turns eating into a true סעודה.

keyTerms.meaning: A cooked dish with gravy or broth (רש"י)
Said in the name of רבי יוחנן (passed on through another sage)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Any meal in which there is no cooked dish with gravy
phrases.notes: This follows רש"י's explanation of שריף.

phrases.english: is not a meal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel statement in the same pattern as רב's
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A meal without שריף does not count as a meal.

steps.title: New משנה: the after-blessing for grapes, figs and pomegranates
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל says that after eating grapes, figs or pomegranates, one says all three ברכות of ברכת המזון. The חכמים say one blessing that sums up the three.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone who ate grapes, figs or pomegranates says three blessings afterward. This is the view of רבן גמליאל. The חכמים say: one blessing that summarizes the three.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It asks which blessing to say after eating the special fruits that ארץ ישראל is praised for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל treats these fruits like bread, so they need the full three-blessing ברכת המזון. The חכמים say they need only ברכה אחת מעין שלש, a single blessing that summarizes the three (the one we know as על העץ). The argument is about how much these fruits are like bread.

keyTerms.meaning: The three blessings, meaning the core of ברכת המזון
One blessing summarizing the three (על העץ, על המחיה)

steps.whyThisMatters: The halacha follows the חכמים. That is why we say ברכה אחת מעין שלש (על העץ) after eating the fruits of the שבעת המינים.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
One who ate grapes and figs and pomegranates
recites three blessings after them,
these are the words of Rabban Gamliel.
And the Sages say:
one blessing summarizing the three.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה begins. Its link to what came before is the theme of the fruits of ארץ ישראל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן גמליאל: three full blessings after grapes, figs and pomegranates. חכמים: one blessing summarizing the three.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: even boiled vegetables can require full ברכת המזון
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says that if someone eats boiled vegetables as his main food, he says the three blessings of ברכת המזון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: Even if a person ate boiled vegetables, if that is his main food, he says three blessings over it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא adds a third, broader view. He says the full ברכת המזון is not limited to bread or special fruits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי עקיבא, what matters is whether the food is what feeds you (מְזוֹנוֹ). Even plain boiled vegetables count if they are your real meal. This pushes רבן גמליאל's idea even further.

keyTerms.meaning: His main food, what sustains him

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
Even if he ate boiled vegetables and it is his main food
he recites three blessings over it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: אֲפִילּוּ אָכַל שֶׁלֶק וְהוּא מְזוֹנוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third opinion in the same מחלוקת, even broader than רבן גמליאל's
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any food that is a person's main sustenance, even boiled vegetables, requires the three blessings.

steps.title: The blessing on drinking water
steps.stepSummary: Someone who drinks water to quench thirst says שהכל נהיה בדברו. רבי טרפון says he says בורא נפשות רבות וחסרונן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who drinks water because he is thirsty says: "שהכל נהיה בדברו" (that everything came to be by His word). רבי טרפון says: "בורא נפשות רבות וחסרונן" (who creates many living beings and their needs).
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes with a separate rule about water. It names the blessing, and רבי טרפון gives a different blessing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Water is not a fruit or a grain, so it gets the general blessing שהכל. רבי טרפון says the right blessing is בורא נפשות. The word לִצְמָאוֹ (for his thirst) suggests that drinking for a different reason may be different.

keyTerms.meaning: For his thirst, to quench thirst
That everything came to be by His word, the general blessing
Who creates many living beings and their needs

steps.confusionAlert: Don't skip the word לִצְמָאוֹ. The משנה is talking about someone actually drinking because he is thirsty. The גמרא explains what this word comes to exclude on the next amud.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה sets out levels of blessings: full ברכת המזון, ברכה אחת מעין שלש, and the general blessings for things like water. Each opinion places foods on different levels.

phrases.english: One who drinks water for his thirst
recites: "By whose word all things came to be."
Rabbi Tarfon says:
"Who creates many living beings and their needs."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new law in the same משנה, moving from fruits to water
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Water drunk for thirst gets שהכל according to the תנא קמא. רבי טרפון says בורא נפשות רבות וחסרונן.

steps.title: What is רבן גמליאל's source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins and asks for the reason behind רבן גמליאל's ruling that grapes, figs and pomegranates need all three ברכות of ברכת המזון.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the reason of רבן גמליאל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא section starts by asking where רבן גמליאל gets his ruling from. This sets up the next step, where the answer comes from פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה (Step 16), רבן גמליאל said fruits of the שבעת המינים need full ברכת המזון. That is a big claim, because normally only bread gets the full three ברכות. So the גמרא wants to see his source in the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion section that comes after the משנה
What is the reason? (asks for a source or logic)
The תנא who requires full ברכת המזון after fruits of the שבעת המינים

phrases.english: Gemara:
phrases.notes: Marks the start of the גמרא on this משנה

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabban Gamliel?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the list of rulings in the משנה to analyzing the first מחלוקת
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural basis for requiring three ברכות after the fruits of the שבעת המינים

steps.title: Three verses read together
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל links the verse praising the land's fruits, the verse about bread, and 'ואכלת ושבעת וברכת', so the fruits also get full ברכת המזון.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'A land of wheat and barley, etc.', and it is written: 'A land where you will eat bread without scarcity, etc.', and it is written: 'You will eat and be satisfied and bless ה׳ your God.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with three פסוקים in a row from דברים ח. For רבן גמליאל they form one flowing passage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first verse lists the fruits of ארץ ישראל: grapes, figs, pomegranates and others. The command 'ואכלת ושבעת וברכת' comes right after, so רבן גמליאל applies it to those fruits too. Since this מצוה is the source of the full ברכת המזון, the fruits get all three ברכות.

keyTerms.meaning: A land of wheat and barley: the verse listing the שבעת המינים
You will eat, be satisfied, and bless: the source of ברכת המזון

phrases.english: As it is written: 'A land of wheat and barley, etc.',
phrases.notes: דברים ח:ח, which continues with vines, figs, pomegranates, olive oil and honey

phrases.english: and it is written: 'A land in which, without scarcity,'
phrases.notes: דברים ח:ט

phrases.english: you will eat bread, etc.',
and it is written: 'And you will eat and be satisfied
phrases.notes: דברים ח:י

phrases.english: and you shall bless the Lord your God.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 19
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The three פסוקים form one unit, so the command to bless also covers the fruits listed in the first verse.

steps.title: The חכמים: the second 'ארץ' is a break
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say the verse starting a new 'ארץ' (about bread) breaks off the topic, so 'וברכת' refers only to bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? 'ארץ' interrupted the topic.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the חכמים read the same פסוקים differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second verse opens with the word 'ארץ' again, which starts a new topic. So the fruits belong to the first topic, and the command to bless belongs only to the bread topic. That is why fruits get only one summarizing ברכה, not full ברכת המזון.

keyTerms.meaning: Interrupted the topic, made a break

phrases.english: And the Rabbis [what do they say]?
'Land' interrupted the topic.
phrases.notes: The repeated word 'ארץ' in דברים ח:ט marks a new topic

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the חכמים' reading of the verses quoted in Step 20
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second 'ארץ' separates the fruits from the command to bless, so only bread needs full ברכת המזון.

steps.title: Doesn't רבן גמליאל also see the break?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבן גמליאל ignores the break made by the second 'ארץ'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for רבן גמליאל too, 'ארץ' interrupted the topic!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבן גמליאל. The extra word 'ארץ' is in the verse for everyone, so how can he link the fruits to the command to bless?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים' reading is based on a plain feature of the text. רבן גמליאל cannot just ignore it, so he must explain what the second 'ארץ' teaches according to him.

phrases.english: And for Rabban Gamliel as well,
doesn't 'land' interrupt the topic?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the חכמים' point from Step 21 against רבן גמליאל's derivation in Step 20
steps.kashyaTarget: רבן גמליאל's reading of the three verses as one unit
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The second 'ארץ' is a break in the text that everyone must account for. If it separates the topics, the fruits should not be included in 'וברכת'.

steps.title: The break excludes one who chews raw wheat
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל uses the break for another purpose: someone who chews raw wheat kernels does not say ברכת המזון.
steps.simpleTranslation: That word is needed to exclude one who chews raw wheat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבן גמליאל does use the break, but for a different lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבן גמליאל, the break separates 'wheat' in the first verse from proper 'bread' in the second. It teaches that chewing raw wheat does not count as eating bread, so it does not require ברכת המזון. Since the break is used for this, it does not cut the fruits off from the command to bless.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (for a different lesson)
One who chews raw wheat kernels

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree the second 'ארץ' teaches something. They disagree about what it separates: the חכמים say it separates the fruits from 'וברכת', and רבן גמליאל says it only separates raw wheat from bread.
steps.whatToRemember: רבן גמליאל: the fruits of the שבעת המינים get full ברכת המזון, and the second 'ארץ' only excludes raw wheat. The חכמים: the second 'ארץ' limits full ברכת המזון to bread.

phrases.english: That [verse] is needed by him
to exclude one who chews raw wheat.
phrases.notes: Raw wheat kernels are not bread, so there is no ברכת המזון

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא מִבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְמַעוֹטֵי הַכּוֹסֵס אֶת הַחִטָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 22
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redirecting a textual feature to a different lesson
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The break must separate the fruits from the command to bless.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבן גמליאל the break only teaches that chewing raw wheat is not like eating bread.

steps.title: Blessings for the five grains
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא rules that anything made from the five grains gets בורא מיני מזונות before eating and ברכה אחת מעין שלש after.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב בר אידי said in the name of רבי חנינא: anything from the five species, at the start you say 'בורא מיני מזונות' over it, and at the end one blessing that sums up the three.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a practical rule about the ברכות on grain foods that are not bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grain foods like cooked dishes and cakes made from wheat, barley, spelt, oats or rye are not bread. Before eating, they get the special ברכה 'בורא מיני מזונות'. Afterward they do not get full ברכת המזון, only the shortened ברכה אחת מעין שלש, which follows the חכמים' approach.

keyTerms.meaning: The five grains: wheat, barley, spelt, oats, rye
The ברכה before eating grain foods that are not bread
One blessing summarizing the three ברכות of ברכת המזון
At the start (before eating) / at the end (after eating)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אִידִי אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ya'akov bar Idi said that Rabbi Chanina said:
Anything that is from the five species [of grain],
at the start, one recites over it 'Who creates the various kinds of nourishment,'
and at the end, one blessing abridged from the three.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אִידִי אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the scriptural debate to practical rulings on the after-blessing
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Five-grain foods get בורא מיני מזונות before and ברכה אחת מעין שלש after.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practical halacha of מזונות and the after-blessing על המחיה.

steps.title: Blessings for the seven-species fruits
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי rules that fruits of the שבעת המינים get בורא פרי העץ before eating and ברכה אחת מעין שלש after.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר מרי said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי: anything from the seven species, at the start you say 'בורא פרי העץ', and at the end one blessing that sums up the three.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a parallel rule for the special fruits that ארץ ישראל is praised for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before eating, these fruits get the normal fruit ברכה, בורא פרי העץ. Afterward they get the special shortened ברכה מעין שלש, not full ברכת המזון. This matches the חכמים in the משנה against רבן גמליאל.

keyTerms.meaning: The seven species ארץ ישראל is praised for
The ברכה before eating fruit of a tree

steps.whatToRemember: The halacha follows the חכמים. Grain foods (מזונות) and fruits of the שבעת המינים both get the one ברכה מעין שלש afterward, not full ברכת המזון.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר מָרִי אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי:
phrases.english: Rabba bar Mari said that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
Anything that is from the seven species,
at the start, one recites 'Who creates fruit of the tree,'
and at the end, one blessing abridged from the three.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר מָרִי אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel ruling to Step 24, applied to fruits instead of grains
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fruits of the שבעת המינים get בורא פרי העץ before and ברכה אחת מעין שלש after.

steps.title: אביי asks for the wording of the short three-in-one blessing
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רב דימי what the actual text of the בְּרָכָה אַחַת מֵעֵין שָׁלֹשׁ is.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב דימי: What exactly is the 'one blessing that is like three'?
steps.whatsHappening: Right after the rulings that the five grains and the שבעת המינים get a בְּרָכָה אַחַת מֵעֵין שָׁלֹשׁ afterward, אביי asks what the words of that ברכה are. This sets up the next steps, where רב דימי recites the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 24 and 25 named this ברכה but never gave its words. Now the גמרא moves from 'which ברכה do you say' to 'what do you actually say.' The name means one short ברכה that shrinks the three main ideas of ברכת המזון into one.

keyTerms.meaning: One blessing that sums up the themes of the three main ברכות of ברכת המזון
What is it? (asking for a definition or the content of something)

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Dimi:
What is 'one blessing like three'?
phrases.notes: Asking for the actual wording of the blessing mentioned in steps 24 and 25.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the wording of the ברכה just named by רבי חנינא and רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact text of the בְּרָכָה אַחַת מֵעֵין שָׁלֹשׁ.

steps.title: The full wording of the after-blessing for fruits
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי recites the full בְּרָכָה אַחַת מֵעֵין שָׁלֹשׁ said after eating fruits of a tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: For tree fruits you say: 'For the tree and the fruit of the tree, and for the produce of the field, and for the lovely, good and wide land that You gave to our fathers, to eat from its fruit and be full from its goodness. Have mercy, ה׳ our God, on Israel Your people, on ירושלים Your city, on Your מקדש and on Your altar. Rebuild ירושלים, Your holy city, quickly in our days. Bring us up into it and make us happy in it. For You are good and do good to all.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי answers אביי by reciting the version of the ברכה said after fruits like grapes, figs, pomegranates, olives and dates.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The text follows the three main ideas of ברכת המזון in short form. First it thanks for the food and the land (like ברכת הארץ). Then it asks for mercy on ירושלים and the מקדש (like בונה ירושלים). It ends with 'טוב ומטיב,' which echoes the fourth ברכה, הטוב והמטיב.

keyTerms.meaning: A lovely, good and wide land (ארץ ישראל)
Good and does good; a short echo of the ברכה of הטוב והמטיב

steps.confusionAlert: Even though it is called 'one like three,' the text also contains a short hint of the fourth ברכה (טוב ומטיב). The name points to the three ברכות from the תורה. The fourth was added later, but its idea still shows up here.

phrases.english: He said to him: Over fruits of a tree:
'For the tree and for the fruit of the tree,
and for the produce of the field,
and for the lovely, good and wide land
that You gave as an inheritance to our fathers
to eat from its fruit and be full from its goodness.
phrases.notes: This is the short version of ברכת הארץ.

phrases.aramaic: רַחֵם ה׳ אֱלֹהֵינוּ עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל עַמֶּךָ,
phrases.english: Have mercy, ה׳ our God, on Israel Your people,

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל יְרוּשָׁלַיִם עִירֶךָ, וְעַל מִקְדָּשְׁךָ, וְעַל מִזְבְּחֶךָ.
phrases.english: and on Jerusalem Your city, and on Your Temple, and on Your altar.

phrases.aramaic: וְתִבְנֶה יְרוּשָׁלַיִם עִיר קׇדְשְׁךָ בִּמְהֵרָה בְּיָמֵינוּ.
phrases.english: Rebuild Jerusalem, Your holy city, quickly in our days.
phrases.notes: This is the short version of בונה ירושלים.

phrases.english: Bring us up into it, and make us happy in it.
For You are good and do good to all.'
phrases.notes: A short echo of הטוב והמטיב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers אביי's question for the case of fruits.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The full text of the after-blessing for tree fruits.

steps.title: The grain version and its closing line
steps.stepSummary: For the five grains, the opening changes to 'על המחיה ועל הכלכלה,' and the closing is 'על הארץ ועל המחיה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: For the five species of grain you say: 'For the nourishment and for the sustenance and for the produce of the field, etc.' And you close: 'For the land and for the nourishment.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי continues his answer with the grain version. It works the same way as the fruit version but opens with different words, and he also tells us how it closes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the opening words change, from 'tree and fruit' to 'nourishment and sustenance,' because grain foods are filling. The 'כו׳' (etc.) means the rest of the text is the same as the fruit version. The closing names two things together, the land and the food. This sets up the next question about how to close the fruit version.

keyTerms.meaning: The five grains: wheat, barley, spelt, oats and rye
And he closes (the final 'ברוך אתה...' line)

phrases.english: For the five species (of grain):
'For the nourishment and for the sustenance
and for the produce of the field, etc.'
phrases.notes: 'Etc.' means the rest is the same as the fruit version.

phrases.english: And he closes: 'For the land and for the nourishment.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב דימי's answer and covers the grain version.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The grain opening (על המחיה ועל הכלכלה) and closing (על הארץ ועל המחיה).

steps.title: How should the fruit blessing close?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the closing line is for fruits. It brings רב's ראש חודש closing to show that two themes in one closing are possible.
steps.simpleTranslation: As for the closing, how does he close? When רב דימי came, he said: רב would close on ראש חודש, 'Blessed... Who makes holy Israel and the New Moons.' So here, what does one say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks how to word the closing for fruits. It notes that a closing with two ideas is acceptable, since רב did that on ראש חודש. This sets up the answers in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a ברכה should not close on two separate themes. רב דימי reports that רב closed with 'Israel and the New Moons,' which shows two themes can sometimes be joined. So a closing like 'the land and the fruit' is possible, and the question becomes the exact wording for fruits.

keyTerms.meaning: As for the closing, with what does he close?
When he came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
Who makes holy Israel and the New Moons

phrases.english: As for closing, with what does he close?
When Rav Dimi came (from Eretz Yisrael), he said:
Rav would close on Rosh Chodesh:
'Blessed... Who makes holy Israel and the New Moons,'
phrases.notes: An example of a closing that joins two themes.

phrases.english: Here, what (does one say)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The grain closing was given, so now the גמרא asks about the closing for fruits.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The correct closing line of the fruit after-blessing.

steps.title: Two wordings for the fruit closing
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says 'על הארץ ועל פירותיה' (its fruits). רבי יוחנן says 'על הארץ ועל הפירות' (the fruits).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: 'For the land and for its fruits.' רבי יוחנן said: 'For the land and for the fruits.'
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the question, and their wordings differ by one small word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that the closing joins the land and the fruit. The only difference is 'its fruits' versus 'the fruits.' 'Its fruits' ties the fruit to the land itself. 'The fruits' is more general.

phrases.aramaic: רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר: ״עַל הָאָרֶץ וְעַל פֵּירוֹתֶיהָ״.
phrases.english: Rav Chisda said: 'For the land and for its fruits.'

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: ״עַל הָאָרֶץ וְעַל הַפֵּירוֹת״.
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said: 'For the land and for the fruits.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of how to close the fruit ברכה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Two wordings: 'ועל פירותיה' (רב חסדא) and 'ועל הפירות' (רבי יוחנן).

steps.title: No real argument: one wording for us, one for them
steps.stepSummary: רב עמרם says רב חסדא and רבי יוחנן do not really disagree. One wording fits us in בבל and the other fits them in ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עמרם said: They do not disagree. This one is for us, and this one is for them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב עמרם settles the two wordings by saying each is right for a different place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read in the order of step 30, רב חסדא's 'פירותיה' is for 'us' in בבל, and רבי יוחנן's 'הפירות' is for 'them' in ארץ ישראל. Each wording fits a different place. This assignment is challenged in step 32 and flipped in step 33, so the final rule gives 'פירותיה' to ארץ ישראל, not to בבל.

keyTerms.meaning: This one is for us (בבל), and this one is for them (ארץ ישראל)

steps.whatToRemember: רב עמרם's key idea is that the two wordings are not a real argument but depend on place. That idea survives, but his matching of wording to place is reversed in step 33.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not memorize which wording belongs to which place from this line. רב נחמן בר יצחק challenges it in step 32, and the גמרא swaps the opinions in step 33. In practice, the שולחן ערוך rules 'ועל פירותיה' for fruit of ארץ ישראל and 'ועל הפירות' for other fruit.
steps.whyThisMatters: It introduces the idea that the closing of על העץ depends on place. The practical wording comes from the corrected version in step 33.

phrases.english: Rav Amram said: And they do not disagree:
This is for us, and this is for them.
phrases.notes: 'Us' means the people in בבל, and 'them' means the people in ארץ ישראל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the seeming disagreement of step 30 by assigning each wording to a different place.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both wordings are correct. Each one fits a different place: one for בבל and one for ארץ ישראל.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Harmonizing two opinions by assigning each to a different place (ולא פליגי)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב חסדא and רבי יוחנן seem to disagree about the closing words of the fruit ברכה.
steps.terutzMaskana: There is no real dispute. One wording is for בבל and one is for ארץ ישראל. (The next step challenges which wording goes with which place.)

steps.title: How can people in בבל bless on fruits they are not eating?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק challenges the assignment of 'פירותיה' to בבל. He argues that people in בבל would be blessing on the fruits of ארץ ישראל while eating their own fruits.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק strongly objects: They (in ארץ ישראל) eat, and we (in בבל) make the blessing?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק attacks the setup from the last step. That setup had רב חסדא of בבל saying 'פירותיה', meaning 'its fruits', the fruits of ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'פירותיה' means 'the fruits of the land', and the land in this ברכה is ארץ ישראל. If someone in בבל says it, he is thanking ה' for fruits that people in ארץ ישראל are eating, not for the fruit in his own hand. That does not make sense, so the way the two wordings were assigned must be wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: He strongly objected to it (a sharp challenge)
They (here, the people of ארץ ישראל)

steps.confusionAlert: רב נחמן בר יצחק is not rejecting רב עמרם's idea that the two wordings match two places. He only objects to which wording was matched to which place.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקִיף לַהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak strongly objects to it:
phrases.notes: מתקיף signals a forceful challenge.

phrases.english: They (in Eretz Yisrael) eat, and we (in Babylonia) bless?!
phrases.notes: Saying 'its fruits' in בבל would mean thanking for the fruit of ארץ ישראל while eating fruit of בבל.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקִיף לַהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the matching of wordings to places from step 31
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רב חסדא in בבל says 'על הארץ ועל פירותיה'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'פירותיה' refers to the fruits of ארץ ישראל. Someone in בבל is not eating those fruits, so he cannot properly bless with that wording.

steps.title: Reverse the opinions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא switches the two opinions. רב חסדא in בבל says 'הפירות', and רבי יוחנן in ארץ ישראל says 'פירותיה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, reverse it: רב חסדא said 'for the land and for the fruits.' רבי יוחנן said 'for the land and for its fruits.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the problem from step 32 by swapping who said which wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now each wording fits its place. In ארץ ישראל people really are eating the land's own fruit, so רבי יוחנן says 'פירותיה' (its fruits). In בבל the fruit did not grow in ארץ ישראל, so רב חסדא uses the general 'הפירות' (the fruits).

keyTerms.meaning: For its fruits (the land's own fruits)

steps.whatToRemember: Final wording: in ארץ ישראל, for fruit of the land, close with 'על הארץ ועל פירותיה'. Outside ארץ ישראל, close with 'על הארץ ועל הפירות'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the closing of the ברכה מעין שלש can change depending on where you are and where the fruit grew.

phrases.english: Rather, reverse it:
phrases.notes: Swap the attributions of the two opinions.

phrases.aramaic: רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר ״עַל הָאָרֶץ וְעַל הַפֵּירוֹת״,
phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said: 'For the land and for the fruits,'
phrases.notes: רב חסדא lived in בבל, so he uses the general wording.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר ״עַל הָאָרֶץ וְעַל פֵּירוֹתֶיהָ״.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said: 'For the land and for its fruits.'
phrases.notes: רבי יוחנן lived in ארץ ישראל, where people eat the land's own fruit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the objection in step 32 by swapping the attributions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב חסדא of בבל said 'פירותיה' and רבי יוחנן of ארץ ישראל said 'הפירות'.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב חסדא of בבל says 'הפירות' and רבי יוחנן of ארץ ישראל says 'פירותיה', so each wording fits the place where it is said.
